title: Compound Measures & Percentages
welcome_lead: Time for the exam-style stretch: density and pressure, best-buy comparisons, and reverse percentages.
meta_desc: GCSE Maths exam-style compound measures — density, pressure, best-buy unit comparisons and reverse percentages.
final_note: You can handle density, pressure, best-buy questions and reverse percentages — top-band ratio skills!

concepts.def: Mass per unit volume: density = mass ÷ volume
Force per unit area: pressure = force ÷ area
The option with the lowest price per unit
A decimal for percent change, e.g. 1.2 or 0.8
Find original from a price after a percent change

walkthroughs.body_html:
Both are compound measures — a rate of one quantity against another.

Density = mass ÷ volume. If 200 g of metal fills 50 cm³, density = 200 ÷ 50 = 4 g/cm³.

Pressure = force ÷ area. A 60 N force on 3 m² gives 60 ÷ 3 = 20 N/m² (= 20 pascals).

Rearrange like speed: mass = density × volume; force = pressure × area.

To decide which deal is best, find the price per unit (per gram, per litre, per item) for each.

Example: 500 g for £3.00 → £3 ÷ 500 = £0.006 per g, i.e. 0.6 p/g.

Compare with: 800 g for £4.40 → £4.40 ÷ 800 = £0.0055 per g, i.e. 0.55 p/g.

The 800 g pack is cheaper per gram → better buy.

If a jumper costs £48 after a 20% discount, what was the original price?

£48 represents (100% − 20%) = 80% of the original. So 80% = £48, meaning 1% = £48 ÷ 80 = £0.60.

Original = 100% = £0.60 × 100 = £60.

Quick check: 20% of £60 = £12, and £60 − £12 = £48. ✓

mcqs.q: A block has mass 150 g and volume 30 cm³. What is its density?
After a 25% increase, a phone costs £250. What was the original price?

numericals.q: Pack A: 400 g for £2.40. Pack B: 600 g for £3.30. Best buy is whichever is cheaper per gram, in pence. What is the price per gram of pack B, in pence?

free_texts.q: A coat costs £36 after a 40% discount. What was the original price in pounds? Just the number (e.g. 50).
